purpose: Four new creature/construct proposals and two developments of included favourites
lore_guardrail: Opaline Kin are excluded from lore. Dawnsail, Coalback, Reedcrown and Alderkin are catalogued; Stonehorn remains developing. New taxa and new ecology/behaviour are proposed.

images.title: Raincup at First Light
images.description: A small dry-country animal with flexible cup-forming frills that gather dew; its water-collecting anatomy gives it a place along old caravan roads.
images.brief:
A RAINCUP, about the size of a large hand, gathering the morning's dew at the edge of a dry caravan trail. Invent a squat soft-bodied amphibian-like creature with four short padded legs, a long balancing tail, a blunt little muzzle and small natural dark eyes. Behind its head grow several broad supple skin frills that can fold together into an upward-facing cup. They are pale jade and translucent at the edges, like living fins, not literal leaves or flowers. The lower body is warm sandy cream with muted terracotta patches.

Catch the specific action: crouched on a sun-warmed flat stone, head turned toward the RIGHT, it tilts one folded frill so a single gathered drop runs along a crease toward its mouth. Its whole posture is occupied with this little daily task. One or two other drops catch the light; no shower of jewels. Its four feet grip naturally. The unusual frills are large simple expressive shapes, not lots of filaments or insect antennae.

Low close viewpoint, plenty of breathing room around the creature and its tail. A worn water flask and the soft edge of a rolled blanket in the distance imply a traveller has stopped here. Broad pale red rock, sparse silver grass and a thin opening of morning sky suffice for the setting. Cool turquoise reflected light through the cup meets warm apricot sunlight on stone, with soft plum shadows. Curious and inventive, not a wide-eyed mascot, infant face or scary exotic pet. Use painted planes rather than skin microdetail. No fire or camp cooking scene.

images.title: Slateprowler on the Descent
images.description: A wolf-sized cliff predator with a low flexible body, broad gripping feet and a balancing paddle-tail; an animal whose danger comes from patient movement rather than spectacle.
images.brief:
A SLATEPROWLER cautiously descending a steep broken rock face at violet dusk. Invent a wolf-sized predator with a low sinuous body, four powerful limbs ending in broad gripping toes, a flattened spade-shaped head, two small deep-set amber eyes and a long tapering tail that broadens into a subtle paddle near its tip. Smooth flexible blue-black hide folds broadly at the shoulders and hips. The body can flatten close to stone. No fur, armour plates, wings, antlers or familiar feline face. The jaw stays shut; suggest a dangerous but understandable wild animal through its posture and attention.

A dramatic three-quarter view from behind and above the creature: it descends diagonally toward the lower LEFT, one forefoot feeling for a lower ledge while the other three maintain purchase, tail extending high to the right as a counterweight. Its head is angled toward a faint disturbance beyond the lower edge, off-screen. Keep all four limbs and the full tail readable, without making it a gymnastics pose.

One simple fracture in the cliff reveals depth. The distant gorge is a large soft plum-blue value mass. A last narrow band of dusk light gives one shoulder and the tail a pale silver edge; a tiny patch of dry ochre lichen and the restrained amber eyes keep the cool scene alive. No enormous glowing eyes or mouth, gore, prey, fighting, theatrical fog or ruin panorama. This is the quietly dangerous side of Breachline's ecology. Broad painterly shadow shapes and selected tactile rock strokes, not hyper-detailed monster concept art.

images.title: Tidevault at the Old Harbour
images.description: A colossal shallow-water crustacean-like grazer with a vaulted living shell. Its movements stir the coastal water; fishermen may learn to work around its passage.
images.brief:
A TIDEVAULT crossing a broad shallow bay beside the remains of an old imperial harbour. It is an immense living coastal animal, roughly the height of a great stone hall. Its low soft body is protected by a broad fluted shell that arches upward in two connected natural vaults. The shell is organic pearl-grey and weathered blue-green, not actual masonry, a castle, a turtle city or a ship. Several stout jointed walking limbs emerge beneath it into the surf, while two shorter forelimbs sweep through the shallows as it grazes. Its small sensory feelers and eyes are understated. An original crustacean-like silhouette, weighty and patient rather than threatening.

WIDE SCENE, creature in the middle distance moving RIGHT, partly veiled by sea spray close to the water only. The curved shell catches a warm copper break in an otherwise cool slate sky. The sea's jade and indigo bands, moving foam and the huge limb shadows establish scale. In the lower-left foreground two tiny fishers in a modest wooden boat angle their oars into the animal's receding wake, calmly working at a safe distance. Their faces are just paint marks. A single broken harbour pier at one edge implies history; no city or buildings carried on the creature.

Dynamic late-day light and broad moving-water strokes, quiet but awe-inspiring. Let some far shell edges disappear in atmosphere. One strong silhouette plus the human activity explains how this animal belongs to a lived coastline. No divine halo, magical beam, monstrous teeth, frightened crowd, tsunami or battle. Unusual anatomy should remain physically comprehensible, with limbs meeting the body naturally.

images.title: Spindlejack Mending the Sail
images.description: A compact repair construct with an open spool-shaped body and fine manipulator limbs, proposed as one Artificer design rather than a biological people.
images.brief:
A SPINDLEJACK made by the Artificers, mending a torn sail with a human ferry worker. A cat-sized brass-and-enamel construct, low and compact, with an OPEN spool-shaped torso containing one visible reel of coarse thread. Four light jointed legs brace against the taut canvas and wooden deck, and two finer front manipulators work a shuttle and guide the seam. Its head is only a small angled housing with a single shaded blue glass lens. Brass ribs and a few worn teal enamel panels leave purposeful negative space. No human face, suit of armour, familiar robot silhouette or dense nest of gears. Its anatomy should instantly explain its task.

MEDIUM INTIMATE VIEW from low on the deck: the worker's plain-sleeved arms and upper body hold the two edges of a tear steady, eyes completely absorbed in the seam, while the little construct advances along it and draws one strand taut. The worker is a middle-aged white man with unremarkable natural features painted simply. Both have clear mutually useful actions; no vague pointing or magical gestures.

Strong sunlight passes through the cream sail so it becomes a luminous backdrop. Cool blue river reflections touch brass and the worker's shadowed sleeve. A muted ochre neckcloth and dark burgundy rope coil provide subtle warm colour without turning this into an all-blue Gnosis painting. Only a strip of water and a distant soft bank show the ferry's setting. Original fantasy craft and lively visible brushwork, simple hands, broad canvas folds, a few focused metal highlights. No lamp-lighting experiment, city panorama, printed plans or text.

images.title: Alderkin Winter Shelter
images.kind: New scene for an included people
images.lore_status: Alderkin included; winter behaviour is a proposed development
images.description: An older alderkin shelters a traveller from a winter wind, exploring the people outside the green woodland imagery of their first concept.
images.brief:
An older ALDERKIN creating shelter for a weary traveller during a winter crossing. Retain the living tree people's essential anatomy: an asymmetrical flexible trunk body divided into two root legs, long branch arms with a few grasping root-fingers, a narrow organically grown head with quiet dark knot eyes and no carved human face. This individual has weathered silver bark, a broader bent trunk and bare branchlets with only a few russet leaves. It is alive and attentive, not a dead ent, human in bark armour or monstrous old man.

A still but purposeful scene: the alderkin braces both feet in the snowy verge and bends one long arm and its pliant hanging branches into an arch against the wind. Beneath that makeshift canopy, a small hooded human traveller sits on a pack and cups a modest shaded lantern close. The tree person's other hand steadies a loose travelling cloak against the branches. Its head turns LEFT to watch the weather while its body protects the traveller. Nothing grips or cages the human. No heroic stare at the viewer.

Medium-wide framing with the whole tree person visible. Powder-blue snow and a few broad charcoal tree shapes; wind is suggested by slanted bare grass and the loose cloak, not graphic speed lines. A shaft of low winter sun touches the silver shoulder and a handful of amber leaves; the little lantern gives a second softer warm note beneath. Small patch of clear pale sky, quiet violet shadows. Show character through sheltering posture and environmental relationship. Economical painted shapes, selected bark strokes, no all-over carved texture or giant forest panorama. No summoner marks or invented magical power.

images.title: Dawnsails over the Harvest
images.kind: New scene for a favourite creature
images.lore_status: Dawnsail included; inland migration is a proposed development
images.description: A few Dawnsails cross cultivated land at blue hour, placing the enormous flying creatures within the ordinary lives of the new kingdoms.
images.brief:
DAWNSAILS passing over a broad harvested valley at the end of day. Retain the favourite creature's living whale-like body, small forward sensory lobes, two vast translucent sail-fins supported by a few graceful ribs, gently bowed pale underside and long tapering tail. No ship, dragon, bird or god. One main Dawnsail glides overhead toward the RIGHT, its enormous fins softly backlit by the last warm band of western sky. Two much smaller distant silhouettes establish a passage of animals, not an army. Their method of flight and biology remain mysterious; no visible magic engine or aura.

GRAND LANDSCAPE from low in a wheat stubble field. Two tiny farm workers have paused beside a modest loaded hay cart in the lower-middle foreground. One rests a hand on the cart and looks up; the other stands near a draught animal, also watching. Faces are only a few paint marks. The animal and workers are ordinary, with no weapons or heroic pose. The main Dawnsail's shadow crosses the patchwork of fields; its scale should feel immense without placing a sharp oversized monster head close to the camera.

Colour and light: deep ultramarine and blue-violet cloud masses, muted honey stubble and pale mauve hills. A narrow gold-peach horizon shines through one sail and on the cart's edge, making the membranes quietly luminous through transmitted light rather than neon glow. Plenty of negative space; some distant atmospheric shapes may be abstract and translucent. This shows stable life continuing under the world's wonders after the Silence. No ruined-city skyline, sea cliffs, golden thread, celestial portal, visible god or unrelated spectacle. Broad confident paint, lost edges in the clouds and a clear emotional point of view from the small people below.

current_generation_direction.direction:
CASTING: For new highly aggressive frontline fighters, the vast majority should be men; female soldiers remain occasional. Women remain welcome as mages, archers, civilians and other characters. Preserve specifically approved identities unless the creator requests a change.

FACES: Actively consult the human/species face sheets. Use specific ordinary reference faces for corrective casting, and draw on their varied skulls, noses, jaws, ages and asymmetries when inventing new people. Keep generally appealing faces and occasional exceptional beauty; avoid repeated model faces, compulsory ugliness and uncanny skin detail.

MATERIALS: Skin, wool, wood and stone have naturally diffuse surfaces. Reserve stronger reflections for appropriate metal, glass or water. Avoid waxy faces, uniform surface shine and habitual red cheeks, especially on heavyset women. Keep vibrant color and convincing light.

PAINTED ATTENTION: Match brush size, edge precision and detail locally. Focal features can be precise; secondary people and distant places stay legible with fewer marks and quieter contrast. Do not combine coarse texture with uniformly hairline detail, render everything equally sharply, or substitute camera blur and tunnel focus.

DESIGN RANGE: Constructs may have abstract functional anatomy, asymmetry and open space; they need not resemble armored human knights. Gnosis combines scholarly high fantasy with broader steam-era craft, not an optics uniform. Blend selected Asian armor details into the established kit; modest curved eaves are a valid architectural option. These are examples, not mandatory formulas.

MAGIC AND PRESENTATION: Direct personal and creature magic, imbued objects and industrial applications can coexist without universal equipment, visible power feeds or glowing threads. Keep grounded steam machinery and creature/direct magical flight distinct from the rejected hovering magitech vessels. Choose a compelling image; card rules do not require an ability demonstration.

REFERENCE USE: Accepted references guide anatomy, materials, individual continuity and taste; they do not limit new faces, clothes, kit, settings or magic to a repeating catalog. Preserve accepted content and vary presentation. Feedback applies at the image or batch scope given unless the creator makes it general.
current_generation_direction.usage: This dated file records existing concepts. For new work, use current direction and the latest creator feedback; exact old prompts are provenance. Preserve recorded local approvals and lore status.
